_doc: Hardware-decode integration toolchain provenance. This file is the machine-readable half of matrix category A. tests/hwdecode/sources.py reads it at startup and refuses to run when a binary on disk does not match. Any mismatch is FAIL, never a warning.

policy.note: Hardware decode stays non-default in this integration. The patched binaries are research builds and must not be distributed; they live under tools/avhw/ which release/build_release.py does NOT whitelist.

patch.defect: RC-1: PipelineTaskNVDecode::getOutputFrame() treated the first *fed* packet's PTS as the presentation start and released every buffered picture below it, so open-GOP leading pictures were never emitted.

stock_control.role: negative control: reproduces the N-3 / N-2 head loss. Used by HD-C01 and as the injected failure in HD-C11/HD-F05.

proven_combinations.evidence: research: N-3 -> N at 30/330/10170 frames, byte-identical to --avsw
research: N-2 -> N at 195 frames, byte-identical to --avsw

patch.scope: 15 added lines, 1 line replaced, 2 files (QSVPipeline/qsv_pipeline_ctrl.h +10/-1, QSVPipeline/rgy_input.h +6)
patch.defect: RC-2: PipelineTaskMFXDecode::sendBitstream() rejected every MFX output whose presentation timestamp preceded m_firstPts, and m_decFrameOutCount could not advance while rejections were ongoing, so all such pictures were rejected.

qsv.claim_boundary: Runtime-proven on QSVEncC 8.26 pinned revision; not yet a general claim for later releases. Releases 8.27-8.30 exist and were not examined.

stock_control.role: negative control: reproduces N-3 on Sony and the H.264 4:2:2 capability refusal.

proven_combinations.evidence: research: N-3 -> N, per-frame SHA-256 identical to --avsw (30/30)

known_refusals.evidence: avqsv: codec h264(yuv422p10le) unable to decode by qsv. rc=-31, no reader constructed, no output file. Unchanged by the patch.

build_deviation_note: Both patched binaries are research builds: avs/vpy readers disabled (NVEncC), OpenVINO and avs/vpy readers disabled (QSVEncC), generated CUDA MSBuild shim and dynamically linked FFmpeg (NVEncC), OneVPL built separately (QSVEncC). Consequence for the matrix: cross-binary wall-clock and fps are NOT a controlled benchmark. Cross-binary comparisons in this matrix are correctness-only (counts, PTS, keyframes, fingerprints, bytes).
